title: Payoff and Loan Satisfaction Agreement Signature and Withdrawal Terms
content:
Agreement settings of the Payoff and Loan Satisfaction product, by plan. They govern whether a signed agreement from the borrower or successor is needed before funds or a deed are taken, how long the signer has, and what follows a lapse or a change of mind.

| Setting | Borrower Voluntary Payoff | HECM-to-HECM Refinance Payoff | Heir Retention Payoff | Estate Market Sale Payoff | Approved Short Sale Payoff | Deed in Lieu of Foreclosure |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A signed agreement from the borrower or successor is needed before funds or a deed are taken | no | no | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| Calendar days after terms are issued within which the agreement must be signed | 0 | 0 | 15 | 15 | 15 | 15 |
| A signed agreement can be withdrawn before it completes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| A retaining successor must show proof of funds or a financing commitment before the agreement is issued for signature | no | no | yes | no | no | no |
| What a requester does after a case lapses | opens a new case | opens a new case | opens a new case | opens a new case | opens a new case | opens a new case |

A signature period of 0 days appears only on the two plans that need no signed agreement.

### Settings read as conditions

| Plan family | Agreement needed | Signature period | Proof of funds before the agreement is issued |
|---|---|---|---|
| Borrower Voluntary Payoff, HECM-to-HECM Refinance Payoff | no | none | no |
| Heir Retention Payoff | yes | 15 calendar days | yes |
| Estate Market Sale Payoff, Approved Short Sale Payoff, Deed in Lieu of Foreclosure | yes | 15 calendar days | no |

### Basis questions

**Can a signed agreement still be withdrawn?** Yes, on all six plans, so long as it has not completed.

**What follows a lapse?** On every plan a lapsed case is not revived; the requester opens a new case.
